definition: One run of a random experiment, such as one roll of a die or one spin of a spinner.
One possible result of a trial, such as rolling a $4$.
The set of every possible outcome of a trial, written $U$; $n(U)$ is the number of outcomes in it.
A set of outcomes from the sample space, such as rolling an even number; it happens when the outcome of the trial is in the set.
Outcomes that each have the same chance of happening, as with a fair die or a person chosen at random.
The number of times an event happened divided by the number of trials; it estimates the probability of the event.
An event $A$ and the event $A'$ (not $A$), which holds every outcome in $U$ that is not in $A$; exactly one of them happens, so $\mathrm{P}(A) + \mathrm{P}(A') = 1$.
